contracts.name: Marketplace verify and update form
assumptions: One form covers verifying a listed snapshot and publishing a newer commit; the title prefix is [Verify]:
The update action is the option labelled exactly: Verify and publish a newer upstream commit
The body is six headings in this order: Verification action, Plugin ID, Repository URL, Target commit, Verification acknowledgment, Standard installation acknowledgment
Target commit is a full 40 character sha, and for an update it is the repository's current HEAD

contracts.name: Marketplace new submission form
assumptions: The title prefix is [Plugin]: and the form has six headings and five required acknowledgments
Category is one exact case-sensitive value and tags are one to three values from the listed set

contracts.name: Marketplace submission guide
assumptions: approved-and-verified is the only label that publishes, for new listings and updates; approved-for-listing is a legacy audit label
A failed or corrected request is retried by editing the same issue, never by opening a duplicate
An update keeps the current snapshot live until the new commit is approved

contracts.name: Marketplace verification policy
assumptions: A listing is update-unverified whenever upstream HEAD differs from listingValidatedCommit, including for commits that change no runtime file
Publication refuses if the upstream commit changes after analysis, so HEAD must stay frozen while a request is pending
The install and update commands clone mutable upstream HEAD and are not bound to the verified commit
verificationCoverage in catalog.json is the authoritative state, not the issue labels

contracts.name: Marketplace security baseline
assumptions: review-required with zero findings is the normal state awaiting a maintainer; needs-fixes means a finding blocks promotion
A download in an installer-adjacent script can be reported as curl-pipe-shell even when nothing downloaded is executed
Capabilities such as installer, remote-build and package-manager are reported for maintainer review and are not findings

contracts.name: Omarchy shell and plugin contract
assumptions: A plugin is a repository with a root manifest.json that declares schemaVersion 1 and entryPoints to hosted QML files
Third-party plugin code runs unsandboxed inside the long-running shell process
The plugin directory is watched, and a reload destroys and recreates QML instances

contracts.name: Marketplace repository identity
assumptions: Submissions are filed to this owner/name. It moved from HANCORE-linux to omacom on 2026-08-30 and the old name only redirects
Any tool that recognises a submission by repository name must match this name

contracts.name: Omarchy repository identity
assumptions: The shell and its docs live here; basecamp/omarchy only redirects

contracts.name: Marketplace catalog endpoint
assumptions: The catalog is served here directly with HTTP 200 and no redirect. A plugin that refuses redirects by design cannot load it otherwise
The body is a JSON object with a plugins array

contracts.name: Marketplace stats endpoint
assumptions: Engagement stats are still served from the old domain's API host. The marketplace's own engagement.js calls it in production
The body is a JSON object keyed by plugin id under plugins
consumers: intent-solutions-io/omarchy-plugins: plugins.json marketplace.stats, scripts/catalog_pipeline.py, site/assets/app.js allowedStatsHost

contracts.name: Retired marketplace catalog host
assumptions: The old host answers 301 to plugins.omarchy.org and must not be shipped in a plugin. If this stops being a 301 the old links on the web are dead or have been repointed
